items.title: Poppy Playtime
items.content_text: At Boulevard City, step into the eerie world of Poppy Playtime, where an abandoned toy factory hides sinister secrets. This immersive hide-and-seek horror challenge keeps you on edge as every shadow and corner could be a safe haven—or a trap. Combining suspense, mystery, and thrilling interactive gameplay, Poppy Playtime delivers one of most unforgettable and spine-tingling adventures. Book Now

items.title: Riyadh Season: BLVD City
items.content_text: Boulevard City is one of Riyadh Season’s most iconic entertainment hubs, offering a vibrant mix of attractions, from the dazzling dancing fountain to upscale dining, shopping, theaters, and immersive experiences for all ages. Visitors can explore OLULOU, where a towering dinosaur skeleton offers the perfect photo op, and let kids dive into four imaginative zones at PLAY-TOPIA. For thrill-seekers, Poppy Playtime delivers suspense inside an abandoned toy factory, A Lot Like Life challenges your bravery in a zombie outbreak, and The Conjuring opens October 15 with spine-chilling scenes from the haunted universe of Annabelle. Families can brave the haunted farm at Zeela House, while pop culture lovers enjoy FUNKO (from Nov 15), with giant figures and collectibles, and gamers embark on a real-world adventure inside MINECRAFT (also from Nov 15). Launching December 18, Flying Over Saudi offers a groundbreaking 5D flight experience that takes you on a 7-minute immersive ride above Saudi Arabia’s most iconic landmarks.

items.title: The Groves
items.content_text: The Groves offers a multi-sensory experience that transforms with each season. Every chapter brighter, richer, and more captivating than the last. From immersive dining concepts to live entertainment, art, and nature-inspired design, The Groves Chapter IV unveils new moments of wonder designed to excite, delight, and inspire.

items.title: Immersive Experience: Flying Over Saudi
items.content_text: “Flying Over Saudi” at Boulevard City, Riyadh offers a one-of-a-kind tourism and entertainment experience—the first of its kind in the Kingdom—inviting visitors into a fully immersive theater that engages all five senses through stunning visuals, surround sound, realistic motion, touch, and scent. Enjoy a 7-minute aerial tour that feels like flying, taking you across Saudi Arabia’s most breathtaking natural landscapes and iconic landmarks in an unforgettable, awe-inspiring journey through the Kingdom’s highlights. items.title: Horses and Equestrian Heritage Exhibition
items.content_text: The King Abdulaziz Public Library is hosting a specialized exhibition on horses and equestrian heritage in celebration of Saudi Founding Day. The exhibition showcases a rich collection of manuscripts, rare books, photographs, historical documents, Islamic miniatures, and illustrated works highlighting the deep-rooted equestrian legacy of the Kingdom. Marking four decades of preserving cultural heritage, the library also presents selections from its dedicated Equestrian Center, which houses more than 12,000 rare Arabic and international references on horses, alongside historic photographs captured by Princess Alice of Britain during her 1938 visit to Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Solo Art Exhibition Series
items.content_text: Misk Art Institute presents the third edition of the Solo Series, spotlighting established Saudi artists Fouad Mougharbel and Saad Almasari, whose work has contributed significantly to the Kingdom’s evolving visual culture. Through two individual exhibitions—“Taibah: Remnants and Solace” by Dr. Fouad Mougharbel and “Geometry as Thought” by Saad Almasari—the series offers insight into their artistic journeys and practices, reflecting their sustained engagement with the local art scene. Together, the exhibitions highlight diverse perspectives and approaches that contribute to shaping Saudi Arabia’s contemporary artistic identity. items.title: Hayy Arts | Global Positioning System
items.content_text: Opening May 20, 2026, ‘Global Positioning System’ is an upcoming exhibition curated by Indranjan Banerjee and Lucas Morin. Global Positioning System is an exhibition dedicated to mapping and navigation systems. It tells stories of fast cars and slow trains, street barriers and trembling grounds, warping highways and broken bridges.

items.title: Hayy Arts | Red Wind, Coral Worlds
items.content_text: Opening May 20, 2026, ‘Red Wind, Coral Worlds’ is an upcoming exhibition curated by recipients of the Art Jameel Curatorial Open Call, Huda Tayob and Miriam Hillawi Abraham. Red Wind, Coral Worlds sites the Red Sea within an expanded and interconnected oceanic terrain. The exhibition traces the entangled worlds that converge across its waters, attending to the material and affective remnants left in the wake of centuries of movement and migration shaped by trade, pilgrimage, and displacement.

items.title: Hayy Learning | Recess: An After-School Programme for Teens
items.content_text: Recess is back — and applications are open! An alternative afterschool arts programme at Hayy Jameel for ambitious teens aged 14–17. Over 12 weekly sessions, participants dive into contemporary art through studio practice, research, field trips to local galleries and artist studios and mentorship from working creatives. Every student hand-binds their own portfolio throughout the programme, and the whole cohort comes together at the end for a real, student-led showcase.

items.title: Art Futures Camp 2026 – Diriyah Art Futures
items.content_text: Art Futures Summer Camp for Arabic-Speaking Teens is a three-week immersive programme hosted by Diriyah Art Futures (DAF), the MENA region’s first centre dedicated to New Media Arts. Designed for Arabic-speaking teens aged 14–18, the camp offers an in-depth introduction to digital art practices in a dynamic and supportive environment. Under the 2026 theme, “Digital Art and Portraiture,” participants explore new ways of representing identity in the digital age, questioning how individuals are portrayed when faces become data and images circulate beyond physical presence. The programme combines creative experimentation with foundational technical skills, including Fab Lab practices and digital studio portraiture. Throughout the camp, participants work closely with industry specialists and creative mentors, culminating in a collaborative exhibition produced with DAF’s curatorial and exhibition teams to showcase their work. Applications are officially open, with aspiring young creatives in Riyadh able to apply until Sunday, June 7.

Through creative expression, the exhibition highlights the dialogue between past, present, and future, reflecting the dynamic role of art in shaping and interpreting social change.

items.content_text: تطلق جامعة الجوف البرنامج الصيفي بجامعة الجوف 1447هـ – 2026م، بوصفه برنامجًا نوعيًا متكاملًا يستهدف تنمية المهارات وتطويرها، ونشر ثقافة الابتكار، وترسيخ ثقافة التطوع وخدمة المجتمع، بما يعزز دور الجامعة التنموي والمجتمعي، ويفتح مسارات واسعة لاستثمار فترة الصيف في برامج معرفية وتدريبية وتطوعية ورياضية موجهة لمنسوبي الجامعة وطلبتها والخريجين وأفراد المجتمع. ويستهدف البرنامج، الذي يمتد من شهر يوليو حتى نهاية أغسطس 2026م، أكثر من 16,000مستفيد من داخل الجامعة وخارجها، من خلال أكثر من 50 برنامجًا وفعالية نوعية، وما يزيد على 210 ساعة تدريبية مكثفة، إلى جانب مشاركة أكثر من 300 متطوع أكاديمي وطبي، وتنفيذ أكثر من 11,000 ساعة تطوعية معتمدة، إضافة إلى أكثر من 10 بطولات رياضية صيفية.

items.title: Build & Play Together
items.content_text: A guided activity space where children take part in simple building tasks, group play, and short storytelling moments. The program introduces simple ideas about homes and daily life across cultures through hands-on participation.

items.title: Echoes of the Familiar
items.content_text: Echoes of the Familiar exhibition explores the concept that home transcends mere physical space, embodying a tapestry of memories intricately woven into its very walls. It is within these confines that the echoes of laughter from childhood games intermingle with the remnants of disagreements and tears shed upon pillows. Each drawer brims with knick-knacks whose purposes remain elusive yet evoke nostalgia. The scent of maternal cooking and the rhythmic snoring of a father create a comforting ambiance, while the presence of a grandmother before the television grounds us in familial continuity. These shared experiences resonate universally, forging a collective nostalgia for "al zaman al Jameel

items.title: Tafasahu: Make Room
items.content_text: Tafasahu: Make Room is an exhibition that showcases a commissioned installation by Saudi architect and artist, Nada AlMulla, which invites you to enter as a guest—to pause, gather and reflect on the conditions of belonging within the context of the traditional Majlis, Arabic for "gathering space." Beyond being a place to receive and host guests, the Majlis has been a vessel for the transmission of knowledge and heritage. The installation deconstructs this space into its essential elements while centering stories, memories and subtle traces of everyday life that animated it: conversations shared over coffee, the lingering scent of incense, the rhythms of gathering and departure. Hospita

items.title: Leap Then Look!
items.content_text: An intractive exhibition that encourages play and collabration, Inviting visitors to assemble and combine different aculptures to create a collaborative artwork while exploring the senses and imagination.

items.title: Beaded plant Suncatcher
items.content_text: Sunlight has a way of bringing a space to life. As it passes through a window, it fills a room with color, movement, and small moments that make a house feel like home. In this workshop, participants create beaded plant sun catchers inspired by the light that streams through our windows and the natural elements we welcome into our homes. By combining colorful beads and delicate forms, each piece is designed to catch and reflect sunlight, creating shifting patterns of color and light. The result is a decorative artwork that celebrates the warmth of home through nature, color, and light.

items.title: Puppet World
items.content_text: Step into Puppet World, a magical roaming experience where giant luminous puppets come to life, transforming Children's festival into a world of wonder and imagination. wering above the crowd, these illuminated characters gracefully dance, interact with visito and create unforgettable moments for audiences of all ages. Don't miss the chance of attending this parade with family and friends!

items.title: PFL MENA Fight Night
items.content_text: Riyadh is hosting PFL MENA Fight Week, bringing together some of the region's top mixed martial arts (MMA) athletes for an exciting week of competition and fan engagement. The main Professional Fighters League MENA Fight Night will take place on Friday, 10 July, at the Global Theater in Boulevard City. Fighters will share their preparations before completing the official weigh-in ahead of the tournament. Held under the Professional Fighters League (PFL) MENA, the event follows the league's signature "win-and-advance" format, providing Arab athletes with a pathway to compete for championship titles while supporting the growth of mixed martial arts across the Middle East and North Africa. Book Now

items.title: Ajeeb in Wonder House
items.content_text: A story-led experience that follows Ajeeb as he visits a series of unusual homes, each shaped by a different idea, form, or function. As the story unfolds, children observe how each space reflects a way of living, then shift into designing a home that suits Ajeeb himself. The activity combines storytelling with creative decision-making, moving from observation to design.

items.title: 1, 2, 3, A Little Space for Me
items.content_text: Small spaces can hold big discoveries. Designed for children under three with their parents, this environment is divided into three distinct zones: movement, hands-on exploration, and quiet play. Each area offers a different way to engage, from active motion to focused interaction and calm building. The experience supports early development through movement, touch, and shared exploration.

items.title: 1, 2, 3, Let's Rhyme!
items.content_text: Come sing along with us as we explore beloved nursery rhymes, discover new ones, and enjoy a wonderful storytelling experience. Connect with other families in a welcoming environment that promotes early childhood development and provides lots of entertainment. This session, lasting for 30 minutes, is ideal for children aged 0 to 3 years.

items.title: A Home I Imagine
items.content_text: A home can begin as an idea and take shape in many forms. In this workshop, imagination leads the design process. Through drawing, building, and assembling materials, children develop their own vision of a home and translate it into a tangible model. Each creation results in a constructed home that reflects personal ideas and vision.

items.title: Around the Table
items.content_text: An interactive activity where children explore how dining tables bring together different cultural practices. The program introduces a range of customs and habits from around the world, showing how the way people gather, sit, and share meals can differ from one place to another. Through simple role-play, children take part in everyday moments such as greeting others, welcoming guests, and spending time around a table.

items.title: Balloon Shapes Lab
items.content_text: Children twist and shape balloons into different forms, experimenting with how each movement changes the shape. Balloon Shapes Lab ضمن ترفيه وعائلات في الظهران. تبدأ الفعالية ١٠‏/٠٧‏/٢٠٢٦، ٤:٠٠ م وتنتهي ٢٥‏/٠٧‏/٢٠٢٦، ٩:٠٠ م حسب البيانات المتاحة. تتوفر لها صفحة جدول حي تساعد الزائر على متابعة الحالة والوقت أثناء الحضور. المصدر: Ithra Events.

items.title: Built by Nature
items.content_text: A bird’s nest, a termite mound, a shell, each one is carefully built, not by chance, but by need. In this workshop, children observe how living things design their homes, then borrow these ideas to sketch and shape their own. Openings for air, layers for protection, and smart use of materials begin to appear in their designs. What starts in nature slowly turns into a built form.

items.title: Children's Café
items.content_text: Step into the Children’s Café, a truly unique experience created just for your child! A space where little ones can enjoy their very own café moment, designed at their scale, where they choose, create and explore freely. From decorating their treats at the Art Toppings Station to relaxing in a cozy Reading Corner, every detail is made to spark joy and imagination. It’s more than a café... it’s a first-of-its-kind experience where children gain confidence in their creativity.

items.title: Draw Your Story
items.content_text: Drawing is one way to represent spaces, ideas, and everyday life to tell their stories through them. In this open drawing space, children use different materials to create images related to their home, activities, and surroundings.

items.title: Hidden Home Bingo
items.content_text: A simple object at home might have a story that starts far beyond the room it sits in. In this fast-paced bingo challenge, children move through clues and questions, connecting everyday items to the materials behind them. As matches come together, unexpected links appearو turning familiar spaces into something to decode and discover.

items.title: Insightful Spaces
items.content_text: The way we experience a space is shaped by what we feel under our feet, not just what we see. In this sensory journey, children touch different carpeted surfaces, noticing textures, patterns, and subtle changes in sensation. As they explore, they begin to recognize how materials influence comfort, sound and perception in everyday spaces.

items.title: Interactive Exhibit
items.content_text: An open-ended interactive exhibition that invites children to explore, create, and play through hands-on experiences. It encourages curiosity, imagination, and discovery for children and their families.

items.title: Let’s Decorate!
items.content_text: Decorations change depending on the occasion, the place, and the people. At the Inspiration Spot, children get inspired to make different styles to celebrate.

items.title: Mic Moments
items.content_text: Everyday life is full of small details, routines, habits, and traditions that differ from one home to another. In this street mic–style activity, children respond to short, guided questions about their daily life. The format is open and conversational, allowing them to speak, listen, and hear different perspectives in a simple setup.

items.title: Mirror Or Window
items.content_text: Some images reflect what we already know, others reveal something new. In this interactive experience, artworks are explored as shifting viewpoints. Certain scenes echo familiar memories, while others introduce different ways of living and seeing the world. Through guided observation and creative response, children interpret what they see and translate it into visual expression. The experience results in personal interpretations shaped by both recognition and discovery.

items.title: My Family Bouquet
items.content_text: A bouquet grows, one flower at a time. In this hands-on workshop, children begin with simple shapes and watch them take form as each piece is rolled, combined, and built into a flower. Colors are chosen, details are added, and the process repeats, each new bloom adding to the whole. As the bouquet comes together, each flower stands for someone at home, gathered into one arrangement shaped through making and choice.

items.title: Our Place on Earth
items.content_text: A house in the desert is not built like one by the sea, and for good reason. In this experience, children explore how homes respond to their environments, from heat to movement to moisture. This leads into building and testing simple structures, adjusting them to stand against different conditions.

items.title: Painted Faces
items.content_text: What's a festival without facepainting? Children choose from a variety of designs and have them painted using safe, child-friendly colors.

items.title: Treasures in Every Home
items.content_text: Deep within the Earth, metal begins its journey, formed over time and transformed into materials we use every day at home. In this interactive workshop, children follow this journey, then reshape a simple tin container into a new functional object. The activity introduces how materials can be reused and redesigned for new purposes..

items.title: Where We Belong
items.content_text: Look closely at Earth, and it begins to feel like a system that never stops working; air moving, water cycling, living things adapting. In this program, children explore how life continues and changes across different environments, and how organisms adjust to survive over time. The journey then stretches further, looking at how science studies these systems and reimagines them beyond Earth. The experience connects life, environment, and possibility in one continuous story.

items.title: Who Lived Here?
items.content_text: Every landscape shapes the homes built within it. This treasure hunt in Rehlaat Gallery, children follow clues across three environments: desert, mountain, and coast. Each stop reveals a model home designed in response to its surroundings, from materials and structure to layout and function. As they move between locations, children match clues to the correct homes, discovering how climate, terrain, and daily life influence the way people build and live.

items.title: Zoom In
items.content_text: A tiny fragment holds the clue. In this Praise of the Artisan treasure hunt, children begin with a zoomed-in detail taken from a larger artwork, a pattern, texture, or small visual hint. Moving through the space, they search for the full piece, matching what they see up close with what appears on the walls. As the search unfolds, attention shifts to details that are often overlooked, building observation skills through careful looking. Each match reveals the complete artwork behind the fragment.

items.title: In the Home of…
items.content_text: Some homes are easy to recognize. Others leave clues behind. In this interactive library experience, children move through a series of spaces, each one arranged as a “home” shaped by a well-known literary character. Objects, layouts, and small details hint at who might live there. As they explore each corner, children follow prompts and challenges that guide them to observe, connect, and identify the character behind each space. The experience unfolds step by step, turning the library into a trail of clues where stories are discovered through place, detail, and interaction.

items.title: My Little Fort
items.content_text: Many children create small spaces of their own at home—under a table, behind cushions, or inside a blanket fort. In this hands-on activity, children build their own small “fort” using soft materials, shaping a space they can define and arrange. The session ends with a short story connected to the idea of shared spaces and home.

items.title: My Neighbor Totoro
items.content_text: A gentle and magical tale by Studio Ghibli that celebrates the innocence of childhood, the quiet beauty of nature, and the meaning of home found in family. Through the eyes of two sisters who move to the countryside, the story unfolds into a world of forest spirits and unseen friends.

items.title: On This Carpet
items.content_text: in Echoes of the Familiar Gallery, around every corner, a story unfolds. This workshop takes place on a carpet filled with familiar scenes, where everyday moments take shape through storytelling and creative exploration. Children move through these scenes, connecting details, building narratives, and expressing their ideas through drawing and simple story-making. Each visit brings together small moments into a larger picture, shaped by observation, memory, and imagination.

A set of outdoor water-based activities where children move between water games that include pouring, splashing, and balancing tasks.

items.title: The House of Ideas
items.content_text: We begin with a simple question: Where do ideas live? Like us, ideas need a place where they feel safe in a space that inspires them and gives them room to grow. In this experience, we explore the House of Ideas: where we will see how a thought begins, what nurtures it and how we can create spaces that allow it to flourish. By designing a pop-up house inside a notebook, participants build a small, personal world where their ideas can live and take shape. Through cutting, folding and creating, a quiet reflection unfolds: what helps our ideas grow, and where do they truly belong

items.title: Unbox Your Story

Join us for a fun family experience as you discover a new world of stories full with boundless imagination and possibilities. All you have to do is open the box in front of you to reveal the tools and materials within. Begin creating your characters and designing your plot with the various elements available to you. Unleash your creativity and share your new story with those around you!

items.title: Mishkat Summer Camp
items.content_text: Discover the exciting world of science, energy, and innovation at Mishkat Summer Camp 2026, where young learners can explore the future through hands-on experiments, interactive challenges, educational games, and collaborative activities designed to inspire curiosity, creativity, and teamwork. Organised by Mishkat Interactive Center, an initiative of the King Abdullah City for Atomic and Renewable Energy (K.A.CARE), the camp introduces participants to the future of energy while developing STEAM skills through experiential learning. Activities explore topics such as solar, wind, and nuclear energy, hydrogen technologies, the circular carbon economy, artificial intelligence, innovation, and programming, supporting Saudi Vision 2030's goals of building future-ready generations. The programme is free of charge and is open to children aged 10–12 years. Camp Schedule Girls: 12–23 July | Boys: 26 July–6 August | Days: Sunday–Thursday Register Now

Individual AlUla Tour stages will be announced closer to the race date, but previous editions have seen riders traverse routes from Old Town to Harrat Uwayrid and Winter Park to Wirkah Mountain.
